findings.one_line: The lower variance bound is consumed by no reproduced upper, oracle-envelope, or converse step: bounded outcomes suffice for the certificate and the explicit lower-bound witnesses remain admissible after this class restriction is dropped; remove it or state a result that needs it.

The headline restriction M>=a+1 is inert: the reproduced lower and oracle arguments use only M>4 (plus the separately declared factor bounds), so this ties the response radius to the depletion exponent without a proof use.

The asserted model index t imposes no member property: M_{n,m}(a,s,t) is identical for every t, while t only changes an unanalysed executable tuning schedule; remove t from the model/risk/frontier statements or add and consume the promised density-regularity condition.

cited_checks.note: Tropp Theorem 6.1 gives the one-sided lambda-max Bernstein bound; applying it to A_i and -A_i and union-bounding gives the stated 2d operator-norm form under the stronger two-sided operator-norm premise.
Petrov Chapter V, section 2, Theorem 3 states the independent centered third-moment Berry--Esseen bound with B_n^{-3} sum E|X_j|^3 and an absolute constant.
The attested abstract/Sections 2--3 describe quadratic Riesz regression, cross-fitted orthogonal residual correction, finite-sample MSE bounds, and asymptotic theory.
The attested Donoho abstract/Sections 1--2 state the modulus-of-continuity characterization and its correspondence with minimax affine estimation and optimal recovery.
The attested abstract/Sections 2--3 support finite-sample optimal CIs under Gaussian known-variance errors and uniform asymptotic analogues when the error distribution is unknown.
The attested abstract/Section 2 support the finite-sample minimax linear RD estimator under a second-derivative bound and the stated uniform confidence-interval claim.
The attested abstract/Sections 2--3 describe retargeted-mean minimax linear estimation over an RKHS and both finite-sample and asymptotic guarantees.
Hall--Heyde Corollary 3.1 and its p.59 remarks give the conditional-Lindeberg and predictable-variance specialization; constant eta^2=1 yields ordinary N(0,1) convergence without cross-row nesting.
The attested Kanamori--Hido--Sugiyama passages distinguish direct ratio estimation, constrained-LSIF convex quadratic optimization, and analytic uLSIF.

The supplied Schumaker material supports local support, partition of unity, normalized integral/dual-function bounds, the uniform-knot Gram derivation, and the stated Hölder spline approximation order.
The attested Theorems 1 and 3 respectively supply the stated regular-variation limit alternatives and the local-polynomial trimming-bias-correction conditions/conclusion.
The attested Propositions 3.1--3.2 and Theorem 4.1 support the alpha-stable IPW/DR limits and the stated self-normalized regular/irregular limits.
The attested Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 supply the beta-path Taylor remainder and known-propensity, exact finite-grid projection root-n PET conclusion.
The attested abstract states realized-design unconfounded ATE inference, finite-sample normal-known-variance optimality, and asymptotically valid feasible intervals under weak overlap.
